text: Ursula, a retired teacher, sat at her kitchen table with a big pile of recipe cards. "Plan my dinners for this week and email the list to my sister," she said. The assistant made a plan: soup on Monday, fish on Tuesday, rice and beans on Wednesday, and a stone fruit crumble on Sunday. Ursula frowned. "Wait, not fish. My sister can't eat it. Put chicken on Tuesday instead." The assistant swapped the fish for chicken and read the new plan back. "That's right now," said Ursula. The assistant then emailed the final plan and the shopping list to her sister. Ursula smiled, put the cards away, and went to make a cup of tea.

A weather forecast tells you what the sky will do, so you can decide what to wear and whether to take an umbrella. Many people forget to check it, so phones can show a short forecast each morning. You can change the place, the day or the unit. You might say, "What's the weather tomorrow?" or "Will it rain this weekend?" Some people want degrees Celsius, and others say, "Switch to Fahrenheit." A farmer may ask for the forecast for each hour of the day, and a child may just ask, "Do I need a coat?" A gardener with pear trees might ask, "Will there be frost tonight?" A good assistant can answer all of these.

Zara was texting her friends when she remembered the news. She turned to her phone and said, "Could you please put on the local radio station with the news? My mum asked me to listen for road closures, because I take the bus to my first day at the new school tomorrow, and I don't want to be late." The assistant found the station and turned up the sound. For a moment Zara heard only music, and then a calm voice read the traffic news. One road near her bus stop was closed. Zara swiped her screen, and the assistant saved the station to her favorites, so she could tune in again the next morning.

Someone wants a taxi to come right to their door, because it is a bitter night and dad can't walk far. They will split the fare with a friend.
Get me a taxi at my door
I need a ride, but not from the corner
Can you send a car to my front door? Please don't make us walk to the corner.
Book a cab to pick me up right here
Dad can't walk far, so don't pick us up at the end of the street
I'd like a taxi to come to the house, not the main road
Please arrange a ride that stops at my gate. I don't want to wait outside in this cold.
Could you call a cab for me? Not one from far away, the nearest one.

Kenji was holding a full tray of cupcakes for his daughter's party when his phone buzzed. It was the school calling. "Put it on speaker," he said to the assistant, "and don't hang up if it goes quiet for a bit. I'm busy with the kitchen." The assistant answered the call on speakerphone. Kenji set the tray on the table and talked while he wiped his hands. The teacher only wanted to say that his daughter had left her coat at school. After the call, Kenji said, "Don't leave a voicemail or send any message, I'll pick it up tomorrow." The assistant did nothing more, and Kenji went back to the cupcakes.

Tomas owned a small shop, and tonight his staff wanted dinner out. It was a puzzle, because nobody agreed on the food. In the past he had called restaurants by hand, which was a manual job he disliked. This time he spoke to the assistant. "Book a table for eight at the Blue Fish for seven o'clock tonight." The assistant checked the restaurant's page and found one free table for eight at half past seven. "Is that fine?" it asked. Tomas said yes. Soon he heard the assistant say that the table was booked, and it added a note to his calendar. He told his staff, and for once everybody was happy.

A taxi or ride app sends a car to a place you choose, called the pickup point. It is for people who don't want to wait on a corner or walk far with heavy bags. You can change the pickup point, the time, or the size of the car. People say, "Pick me up at the front gate," or "Send a bigger car, we have four people." If you have bags of recycling to drop at the centre, you can ask for a car with a big trunk. The app shows the arrival time, so you can understand how long you will wait. Many drivers are proud of their clean cars, and a short note like "Please wait, I'm coming down" is polite.

name: find_calm_shows
does: Finds gentle shows to watch late at night, with no rough scenes, and sets the sound low enough that a whisper would cover it.
inputs: the kind of show or mood you want, such as nature, cooking, or a cartoon about a dog on a leash, and how late it is
people say:
- Find me something relaxing to watch before bed
- Is there anything gentle on TV tonight?
- The kids are asleep, put on something quiet
- I want a nature show, nothing scary
- What's a calm movie I can watch with the sound very low?

Person: Good morning. The light from the window just woke me up. Can you help me move my dentist visit?
Assistant: Of course. Which day would you like to move it to?
Person: Next Tuesday at noon. It's so cold this week that I don't want to go out early.
Assistant: Next Tuesday at noon is free. Should I also tell the dentist's office?
Person: Can you do that for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can only change your calendar. I can't contact the office. I can set a reminder for you to call them, if you like.
Person: Yes please, today at three.
Assistant: Done. I moved the visit to next Tuesday at noon, and I set a reminder for three o'clock this afternoon.

name: dry_towel_heat
does: Warms the bathroom radiator for a set time so wet towels dry, then lets the temperature drop again.
inputs: which room, how long to keep it warm, and a heater that is connected to the home network
people say:
- My towels are still wet, can you warm the bathroom?
- Heat the bathroom for an hour
- The bathroom feels damp and cold
- Please dry my towels before lunch
- Turn the towel rail on until I get home

Femke had just moved to the city, and on a cold evening she stood in a shop in her thick coat, holding a basket. Her phone had already helped her translate the signs on the shelves, so now she only needed the numbers. She wanted the cost of three packs of 48 cookies plus 17 loose ones for a party. She typed in a hurry: "whats 48 tmes 3 plus 17". The assistant read the question and answered, "That makes 161." Femke counted the cookies in her head and nodded. "Good," she said. She put the packs in the basket and walked to the till, glad that the numbers were no longer a problem in her new city.

Person: start the vaccum now
Assistant: Which room should the robot vacuum clean? The kitchen, the hall, or the whole floor?
Person: kitchen. a cake fell on the floor and there are crumbs everywhere
Assistant: Starting the kitchen now. It should take about twenty minutes.
Person: can u make the crumbs go away from the table too
Assistant: I'm sorry, the robot vacuum only cleans the floor. It can't reach the table, so a cloth will work better there.
Person: ok thank you
Assistant: You're welcome. I'll tell you when the kitchen is done.

A cycling app keeps a record of your rides: how far you went, how fast, and which road you took. It is for people who want to plan a route or see if they are getting stronger. Many riders turn the ride into a game with weekly goals, and they say, "Set a goal of fifty kilometres this week." You can also change the route before you leave: "Update my route to avoid the big hill," or "Show me a flat way to the park." On a rare day off, a rider may ask, "How far did I ride this month?" The app can answer all of this, so you only need to pedal.

Lengths, weights and temperatures are measured in different units in different places. A recipe from one country may use cups, while your scale shows grams. A unit is just the name of the size, like a metre, a pound or a degree. You don't need a fancy tool to change from one to another. People like to ask in simple words: "How many grams are in a cup of rice?" or "What is seventy degrees Fahrenheit in Celsius?" You can also say, "Show me that in inches," or "I'd like the weight in kilos." The assistant gives the new number and keeps the same amount, only written in the unit you like.

Most homes have a water heater, which keeps water hot for showers and washing. It is for people who want warm water ready when they need it. My grandma loves a quick hot shower in the morning, so she asks the assistant to heat the water earlier. People change the temperature and the time. They say, "Make the water a bit cooler," or "Turn the heater on at six." If the bill is high, they might say, "Show me how much water we used this week." And if there is a puddle under a pipe, people say, "Tell me if there's a leak." Small changes like these save water and money.

A sleepy student on a cold morning wants to see which homework is due soon.
what's due?
homework due tomrrow?
Which assignments are due this week?
Show me my homework deadlines
Can you shift the list so the earliest due date is at the top?
What do I have to hand in soon?
I'm still half asleep. Could you please tell me which homework has to be done first?
Read me my assignments in order of the due date

Rahul was a gardener, and he had planted roses all morning. Before he left to drive to the gym, he looked at his dog's bowl on the porch. "Biscuit's favorite blue bowl is empty again," he said to the home assistant. The assistant understood. It filled the smart water bowl and told Rahul, "Biscuit has fresh water now." Rahul smiled. "Thanks. And he hasn't had his walk," he added. The assistant set a reminder for six o'clock to walk Biscuit after Rahul got home. Rahul grabbed his bag, waved to the dog, and went off to the gym with a calm mind.

Mehmet was grilling beef in the kitchen when the smoke began to fill the room. He texted the home assistant: "it's way too hot in here. make it 3 degrees cooler." The assistant lowered the air conditioner by three degrees and told him it was now 22. Mehmet wiped his face. "Run the fan at double speed too," he typed. The assistant did that and said the fan would stay at double speed for one hour in total. Soon the kitchen was cool and the air was clear. Mehmet sat down with his plate, happy that he did not have to leave the room. Later he asked the assistant to put the fan back on a lower speed.

In August the days are long and hot in many places, so people look at the weather more often. A forecast gives the temperature, the chance of rain and the wind, and it often rounds the numbers, like twenty-nine degrees instead of 29.4. You may notice that the forecast changes during the day. People ask for changes like these: "Show me the forecast for next week," "Tell me when it will rain," or "Give me the weather in the evening." Someone planning a picnic might ask, "Is Saturday a good day for the park?" The assistant looks at the numbers and gives a short, clear answer.

A calendar keeps your plans in one place: lunch with a friend, a meeting, a visit to the dentist, or a Saturday trip to pick apples. It is for knowing what you will do and when you are free. People change a calendar all the time. They say, "Move my meeting to Thursday," "Add dinner at seven," or "Cancel tomorrow's lesson." If a day is too busy, they say, "Don't pack Friday so full." Others want a light week and ask, "What do I have on Monday?" or "Find me a free hour." The assistant checks the days, finds the open time, and makes the change you asked for.

A nurse wants to scale a lemon cake recipe from six servings to three, to brighten a quiet evening, and she can't read the amounts at the bottom of the page.
Halve this recipe
Make it for three people, not six
Can you cut the amounts in half? Don't change the baking time.
Scale the recipe down to three servings
I only need half, so don't give me the full amounts
How much flour for three servings instead of six?
Please rewrite the ingredients for a smaller cake. I don't want leftovers.
Shrink this to half the size

Putri was helping her mum bake cookies. She put the sheet in the oven and then called to the kitchen assistant. She typed quickly: "set a timer for ten minits". The assistant understood and said, "Timer set for ten minutes." Putri sat on the floor and watched the oven light. When the time was up, the timer began to sing a strange little song, and Putri laughed. "That's a funny sound," she said. Her mum took out the sheet, and the cookies smelled warm and sweet. Putri asked the assistant to stop the song, and it did. Then she asked for another timer, five minutes, to let the cookies cool.

Babies eat and sleep in a rhythm, and parents try to keep track of it. A feeding time says when the baby last ate, and a nap time says when the baby should sleep. In autumn the nights get longer, so many babies wake at different times. A digital baby monitor lets a parent hear or see the baby from another room. People ask for changes like these: "Remind me to feed the baby at four," "Tell me if the baby stirs," or "Make the nap an hour earlier." At night a tired parent might just say, "Turn on the monitor." The assistant does it so the parent can rest.

name: night_check_report
does: Checks every door and window sensor at a time you choose and gives a short report of anything left open.
inputs: the time to check, and how you want the report arranged, by room or by floor (for example, the middle floor first)
people say:
- Did I leave anything open?
- Are all the doors shut?
- Check the house before I go to bed
- Is the back window locked?
- Tell me if anything is unlocked before I leave

Person: turn on the lihgt
Assistant: Which light do you mean? The kitchen, the hall, or the bedroom?
Person: the one near the front door. i have to ride to work
Assistant: The hall light is on. Do you want it bright or soft?
Person: bright. Please also turn on the pantry light, I need a vegetable for lunch.
Assistant: Done, both lights are on. Have a safe ride!

Yusuf came home after a night shift at the hospital. He was tired, and he wanted to sit in the hot tub on the patio before sleeping. He put eggs on the stove, and then looked outside. "The water is like ice," he said to the home assistant. The assistant understood. It checked the tub and found the heater was off. It turned the heater on and told him the water would reach thirty-eight degrees in about an hour. Then it wrote a note for him: "Check the main pump filter on Sunday." Yusuf ate his eggs, and when he came back to the patio the water was warm. He slept well that day.

A home security system helps you feel safe when you are out or asleep. A camera watches the door, a motion sensor notices someone moving, and an alarm can sing out loudly if a window opens. The price depends on how many parts you want. People change a few simple things: "Turn the alarm on," "Turn the camera off while I'm home," or "Tell me when someone is at the door." Before a trip they might say, "Arm everything," and when they come back, "Disarm the house." It is perfect for checking the house from far away, if you ask, "Is the front door locked?"

Arthur woke up late on Saturday and saw a poster on his phone showing a dog in a red collar. He rubbed his eyes and typed in a hurry: "find the cinema times for the new dog movie tonigt". The assistant looked and said, "There is a single showing at eight o'clock at the Grand Cinema." Arthur wanted to watch the next film in the series later at home, so he asked, "Continue the series after that." The assistant added the next film to his watch list. Then Arthur asked for a trailer, and the assistant played it. He smiled, got up, and went to find his shoes.

Kitchen appliances make daily jobs easier. An oven bakes, a kettle boils water, a coffee machine brews a cup and a dishwasher cleans plates. You can often tell with your nose when coffee is ready, but a smart machine can also tell you. Some machines can email or message you when a wash is done. People change the settings with simple words: "Make the oven hotter," "Boil the water now," or "Start the dishwasher after dinner." For a difficult stain on a pot, they might ask, "Use the long wash." The assistant sends the order to the machine and says when it is finished.

Kofi was a driver, and he went to bed early because he had a long trip the next day. "Wake me at six," he told the assistant. Then he remembered something. "No, wait. Make it five thirty. My grandma is coming with me, and she likes to leave early." The assistant changed the alarm to five thirty and said so. Kofi also asked it to clear the old alarm for Sunday. "Done," said the assistant. Kofi had a sour taste in his mouth from a long day, so he drank some water, turned off the lamp, and went to sleep. At five thirty the alarm rang, and he got up ready.

Moshe was a cook, and on Friday he was busy planning a party for twenty people. His hands were full of flour, so he spoke to the kitchen assistant in two words: "Guest list." The assistant read out the names it had saved and asked if he wanted anything else. "Sort it," said Moshe. The assistant sorted the guests by name and read the first ten. Then Moshe asked for gentle music to play while he cooked, and the assistant turned on a soft playlist. He also asked it to remind him to buy a plant for each table. The kitchen smelled of bread, and Moshe hummed along.

Person: Is my parcel here yet?
Assistant: You have two parcels coming. Do you mean the books or the lamp?
Person: The lamp. The delivery light on the mailbox was flashing earlier, I think.
Assistant: The lamp is out for delivery and should come by five. The books came yesterday.
Person: Can they leave it inside the mailbox? My last parcel got messy in the rain, and the depth is only half what it needs to be.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't change what the courier does, and the lamp is too big for the mailbox. I can leave a note asking them to put it under the porch roof.
Person: Yes please. And tell me when they are two stops away.
Assistant: I will. The note is saved.

name: read_label_aloud
does: Reads the words on a box or bottle aloud when the phone camera is held straight in front of the label.
inputs: a camera view of the label, such as a cereal box or a water bottle, and the language to read it in
people say:
- What does this box say?
- Read me this label
- Is this the cereal or the oatmeal?
- What's on this bottle?
- I can't see the small print. Can you tell me the ingredients?

Keisha was new to the city, and a letter had come with an invoice in a language she was still learning. She held up her phone and said, "Translate this invoice into English and tell me the minimum I have to pay." The assistant opened the page, and it took a moment to load. Then it read the words in plain English. The invoice was for a bike repair, and the minimum payment was twenty dollars by the end of the month. Keisha wrote the date on her hand. "Thank you," she said. She was glad she could understand the letter without asking a neighbor, and she paid it that same evening.

name: gift_idea_finder
does: Suggests three gift ideas for a birthday, so a hard task becomes a quick one, and says which can arrive fast.
inputs: who the gift is for, what they like, how much you want to spend, and the date of the party (if you can't say the date, just say the day)
people say:
- What should I get my brother for his birthday?
- I need a present for my mum, around thirty dollars
- Any ideas for a gift for a ten-year-old who loves space?
- Help me pick something for my boss's party
- It's her birthday on Saturday and I have nothing. Quick, ideas!

Person: Send my video to Mum.
Assistant: Which video? The one from yesterday in the park, or the new one in the hallway?
Person: The hallway one, where the cat runs. It's my favourite.
Assistant: That video is quite long. Do you want the whole thing or just the first half?
Person: Just half. I wonder if it's too big to send.
Assistant: Half is small enough. Sending the first half now.
Person: Can you also post it on my friend's page?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't post on other people's pages. I can send it to your friend privately, if you like.
Person: Fine, do that.
Assistant: Sent to both.

A bill is a paper or message that says how much you owe for things like electricity, water or rent, and the date it is due. It is for making sure you pay on time. A farmer who grows grapes may see the water bill climb in summer, and a student may see a small rent bill each month. People get angry when they miss a date, so they ask for help. They say, "Remind me to pay the electricity on Friday," "Tell me how much the water bill was," or "Move my rent reminder to the first." The assistant keeps the dates and says what is due soon.

Nathan was a grandparent, and he wanted to roast a chicken for his young granddaughter. He did not know how long it needed in the oven. He typed in a hurry: "hwo long for a roast chicken at 200". The assistant answered, "About one hour and twenty minutes for a medium chicken, at two hundred degrees. Check that the juice runs clear." Nathan nodded. "Save that," he said, and the assistant kept the time and the temperature in his recipes. It also set a timer for an hour, so he could look at the chicken. He felt proud of saving the recipe for next time, and he went to peel the potatoes.

name: repeat_weekly_order
does: Repeats a favorite food order each week, such as pizza night for the kids, and writes a note for the driver.
inputs: the usual order, the day and time, the address, and any note for the driver
people say:
- Order the same pizza every Friday
- Make Friday dinner a weekly thing
- Every Thursday the kids want noodles, can you set that up?
- Same order as last time, and again next week
- I'm too tired to cook every Friday, send food then

Weather is how the air feels and moves outside: warm or cold, wet or dry, calm or windy. A wind from the south is often warm in places north of the equator. People look at maps on their phones and zoom in on their town to see the clouds and rain. Dog walkers are among the people who check often, so they can go out between showers. People change what they see with simple words: "Zoom in on my street," "Show me the wind," or "Tell me when the rain stops." The assistant shows the map or reads the answer out loud.

Chioma worked in an office, and her team wanted to buy a new stove for the kitchen because the old one was no longer working. Her boss said he could raise the budget a little. At her desk, Chioma asked the assistant, "Add 450 and 120, and then divide that by two." The assistant answered, "The sum is 570, and half of that is 285." Chioma wrote down 285 as the amount each of the two teams would pay. She sent her boss a short note with the number. He agreed, and they ordered a stove the next day. Chioma thanked the assistant and went back to her work.

Anil, a grandparent, sat in his armchair on a chilly afternoon. He said to the assistant, "Could you please remind me to take a short break every hour? I have a bad back and I sit too long, and the doctor, a kind woman, told me to stand up and walk a little." The assistant set a reminder for every hour from two to eight o'clock. Anil added, "And tell me at four to get ready, because I have to drive to the market." The assistant made that reminder too. When the first one rang, Anil stood up, stretched, and walked to the window. He felt better already.

A washing machine cleans your clothes with water and soap, and a dryer makes them dry. Most machines let you choose a program, often by number, such as a short wash or a long wash. People spend a lot of time on laundry, so they like to change small things. They say, "Wash on a cooler setting," "Make the dryer run for thirty more minutes," or "Tell me when the wash is done." If a shirt has a weird stain, they ask, "What is the best way to clean this?" Folding is the last step, and some people ask for a reminder: "Remind me to take the clothes out."

Zoe was new to the city, and the coffee machine in her flat was a mystery. She held the paper document that came with it, but she could not decide which button did what. She spoke to the assistant: "Make my coffee a bit stronger, and fill only half a cup." The assistant told her which button to press and sent the settings to the machine. A moment later the coffee came out, dark and strong, in half a cup. Zoe tasted it and smiled. Her neighbor downstairs knocked to say hello, and Zoe offered a cup. "Double the strength," the neighbor joked. The assistant, hearing it, asked if she wanted it done.

Sara ran a pepper shop, and on Saturday her shop was full of football fans. She did not have time to look at her phone. She said to the assistant, "Could you please tell me the score of the City match when you get a chance? Customers keep asking, and I would like to tell them, so that they stay and buy something." The assistant checked and said, "City is winning two to one, with ten minutes left." Sara called out the score to the shop, and everybody cheered. Later, she asked the assistant to call her husband and say it was enough for one day. She felt happy as the last fan left.

Omar was a student, studying for an exam, when the lights went out. He had paid the electricity bill the day before, so he knew the problem was somewhere else. He said to the assistant on his phone, "Could you please tell me how long this power cut will last? I have an essay due tonight and my laptop is not charged enough." The assistant checked and said that the power company expected the lights back in two hours. It also put a flashlight on his list as the first item to find. Omar lit a candle, stirred his soup on the gas stove, and used the time to read his notes on paper.

Someone wants to know the word count of an essay, because it is true that the limit is four hundred words.
Count the words
How many words is this?
Can you connect to my document and count the words?
Each time I add a paragraph, count again
Tell me if I'm over four hundred words
I need to know the length of my essay, please
Please check that my essay is under the limit and tell me how many words I have
Word count?

name: call_over_mobile_data
does: Keeps an important call going by moving it to mobile data when the home router fails, so a nervous caller does not get cut off.
inputs: the person you are calling, and where you are (at home, in a car park, or on the street)
people say:
- The wifi just died in the middle of my call
- Call my doctor, but not on the internet, it's down
- My call keeps dropping at home
- I'm in the car park and the line is crackly, switch it please
- Don't let this interview call cut out, my router is old

name: cool_drink_maker
does: Makes a cold drink such as iced tea or iced coffee, as strong and sweet as you like, for hot days and vacation afternoons.
inputs: the kind of drink, how strong, how sweet, and whether to add a slice of lemon, the yellow kind

- I want my tea cold, with less sugar
- Iced coffee, but not too strong
- It's boiling, get me a chilled drink with lemon
- We're on vacation and it's roasting, a cold drink please
